expectations.text: Adds an exported camelCase executor to repairTools.js whose second argument is an injectable options object defaulting the retriever (e.g. { retrieve = retrieveRelevantChunks } = {})
expectations.evidence: export function lookupTorqueSpec({ part = "", limit = 5 } = {}, { retrieve = retrieveRelevantChunks } = {}).

expectations.text: Does NOT call retrieveRelevantChunks directly inside the executor body bypassing the injected parameter
expectations.evidence: Body calls the injected `retrieve(query, { limit })`, never the import directly.

expectations.text: Adds a JSON schema entry to repairToolSchemas with a snake_case name and additionalProperties:false
expectations.evidence: name: "lookup_torque_spec", additionalProperties: false, with part + limit params.

expectations.text: Registers the tool in createToolRegistry passing the injected dependency (e.g. (args) => fn(args, { retrieve }))
Adds a unit test in repairPlanner.test.js that injects a mock retriever instead of hitting the real one (mirrors the search_repair_docs test)
expectations.evidence: lookupTorqueSpec({...}, { retrieve: mockRetrieve }) test + a missing-part safe-shape test.

expectations.text: The executor returns a plain JSON-serializable object and tolerates missing args without throwing
expectations.evidence: Returns { part, snippets, context }; blank/missing part returns { part: "", snippets: [], context: "" }.

expectations.text: Adds a step to AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS and a row in the docs/repair-planner.md Tools table
expectations.evidence: AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS step 5 added; docs Tools-table row + checklist item added.

eval_feedback.overall: DI convention followed correctly. Also added a TorqueSpecsPanel + artifact accumulation (beyond the literal ask of 'return snippets') — reasonable, since the data is user-facing, but arguably mild scope creep.
